items.summary: Ordningen i Lier har vært basert på gjentatte dispansasjoner til Viken Skog. Men nå forlanger kommunen at tømmeret skal bort.

items.title: Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
items.summary: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

items.title: Trappar opp kampen mot ulovleg droneflyging
items.summary: Pilotar, politi og ordførar møtest i dag for å finne ut korleis fleire kan bli tatt for ulovleg droneflyging og kven som eigentleg har ansvaret.

items.title: UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
items.summary: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

items.title: US public workers are fighting to protect their jobs from AI – and some are winning
items.summary: As governments adopt AI, workers are gaining ground in how it’s used and securing safeguards against its harms In the shadow of Silicon Valley, workers for the city of Oakland, California, worry the region will deploy AI systems that could increase surveillance and inaccurately evaluate their performance. items.title: Andreeva beats world number two Sabalenka to reach WTA semis
items.summary: Russia's Mirra Andreeva beats world number two and second seed Aryna Sabalenka 6-4 6-0 to reach the last four of the WTA Finals.

items.title: How much art does your council own and is it locked away or on display?
items.summary: More than 500,000 pieces of art are owned by 225 councils, the BBC finds, but most of it is storage.
